issues.legal_issue: Property allotted to a woman in lieu of maintenance and held by her when the succession law commenced became her absolute property under the general enlargement provision rather than remaining a restricted estate under the exception for newly created rights.
material_facts: The woman was allotted the disputed properties in a family settlement in lieu of her claim for maintenance and residence.
The lower courts found that she remained in possession of the properties when the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 came into force.
The defendants’ claim that she had surrendered possession in exchange for annual maintenance payments was rejected by the lower courts.
The courts below held that the allotment recognized her pre-existing maintenance right and that she acquired an absolute interest.
issues.conclusion: The allotment fell under Section 14(1), not Section 14(2), of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956; the woman acquired an absolute interest in the properties, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1) and its Explanation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, property possessed by a Hindu woman and received in lieu of maintenance in recognition of a pre-existing right becomes her absolute property. Section 14(2) does not apply to such an allotment. The Court agreed with the High Court for the reasons given in Civil Appeal No. 1360 of 1968, heard along with this appeal; the judgment also identifies the matter as an appeal concerning Chellammal v. Nellammal.

predicates.appeal_challenges_womans_property_intere: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a ruling on a woman's interest in property allotted to her.
predicates.property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance: The property was given to the woman in recognition of her claim to maintenance.
predicates.holder_possessed_property_when_successio: The woman held possession of the property when the succession law commenced.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a woman's property interest, the property was given to her in recognition of maintenance, and she possessed it when the succession law commenced, she acquires an absolute property interest.
